chunks: "Do not recite poetry at night, and do not recite it during the nights or days of the month of Ramadan." Isma'il said to him, "O my father, even if it is about us?" He عليه السلام said, "Even if it is about us."

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ: Isma'il, the questioner in the report
key_terms.فِينَا: about us, meaning concerning the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to recite poetry at night or during the month of Ramadan in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs that poetry should not be recited at night, nor during the night or day in the month of Ramadan. When Isma'il asks whether this also applies to poetry concerning the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, the Imam affirms that it does, showing the special etiquette and restraint expected in these sacred times.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1859 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Do not recite poetry at night, and do not recite it during the nights or days of Month of Ramadan."
Isma'il then asked him, "O my father, even if it is about us?"
Imam (as) replied, "Even if it is about us."
